m.n: The Sacrament of Confirmation & Gifts of the Holy Spirit

co.n: The Sacrament of Confirmation & Gifts of the Holy Spirit Cohort

c.p: What is the theological purpose and effect of the Sacrament of Confirmation?
c.a: an outpouring of the holy spirit to strengthen baptismal grace and empower apostolic witness | strengthening baptismal grace with the holy spirit | outpouring of the holy spirit to witness to christ
c.h: Just as at Pentecost, it deepens the presence of the Holy Spirit so the believer can defend and spread the faith.
c.e: Confirmation perfects baptismal grace, uniting us more firmly to Christ, increasing the gifts of the Holy Spirit, and giving special strength to spread and defend the faith (CCC 1285, 1302–1303).
r: graduation from religious education meaning you never have church again
Confirmation is not a graduation or exit, but the beginning of adult apostolic responsibility and active service in Christ's Church.

c.p: Name the Seven Gifts of the Holy Spirit bestowed in Confirmation (Isaiah 11:1-2).
c.a: wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety, and fear of the lord | wisdom understanding counsel fortitude knowledge piety fear of the lord | wisdom fortitude knowledge piety counsel understanding and fear of the lord
c.h: These gifts assist our mind, will, courage, and reverence toward God.
c.e: The seven gifts of the Holy Spirit (Wisdom, Understanding, Counsel, Fortitude, Knowledge, Piety, and Fear of the Lord) sustain and enrich the moral and spiritual life of Christians (CCC 1830–1831).
r: wealth, fame, pride, power, ambition, physical strength, and success
These are worldly desires; the spiritual gifts of the Holy Spirit cultivate holiness, virtue, humility, and love of God.

c.p: What sacred matter is used by the bishop during the anointing on the forehead at Confirmation?
c.a: sacred chrism | chrism oil | holy chrism
c.h: A fragrant mixture of pure olive oil and sweet balsam consecrated during the Holy Week Chrism Mass.
c.e: The Bishop anoints the candidate's forehead with Sacred Chrism while laying on hands, saying: "Be sealed with the Gift of the Holy Spirit" (CCC 1295–1300).
r: The Church specifically requires Sacred Chrism, which is consecrated by the diocesan bishop with fragrant balsam to symbolize the aroma of Christ.
